Red brick vs AAC block: how should you compare them?

Walling choice affects dead load, labour, chasing, plaster, fixing details, thermal behaviour and execution. The right option depends on the structural and architectural design, local workmanship and project priorities.

Compare red clay brick and AAC block for house construction by weight, workmanship, services, plastering, moisture detailing and project-specific suitability.

Start your requirement · Find professionals

01

Compare the complete wall system

Unit price alone misses mortar/adhesive, plaster thickness, wastage, labour productivity, chasing, lintels, fixings and waterproofing details.

02

Weight can influence the structural system

AAC is generally lighter than conventional clay masonry units, but wall type and load assumptions must be coordinated with the structural design.

03

Workmanship changes the outcome

Poor jointing, improper curing where required, careless chasing and weak junction detailing can create cracking or finishing problems with any walling system.

04

Plan service chases and heavy fixings

Electrical/plumbing routes and wall-mounted loads should be planned early. Use appropriate anchors/fixing systems for the selected substrate.

05

Ask for one written wall specification

Define unit type, dimensions, mortar/adhesive, reinforcement/mesh at junctions where specified, plaster system and external-water protection before comparing quotes.
